mechanism_narrative: The continued week-to-week recovery in WORKPLACES mobility raises weekday spillover demand for nearby shopping and dining, so RETAIL_REC should move higher over the next four weeks as commuting-linked foot traffic rebuilds.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -20.6 to -11.7 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to improve but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below its last-28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain suppressed, more activity is displaced into home-based routines and discretionary retail visits weaken; this should keep RETAIL_REC flat to lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +4 while WORKPLACES stays below -10 for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If the residential-workplace gap persists for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior two-week average, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below its recent level signals tightening movement frictions that suppress spontaneous retail trips within one week, pushing RETAIL_REC lower.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -2 after being above -1 in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -0.4 at t-2w to -1.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -2 but RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to hold above +20, routine errand traffic remains concentrated in essential trips rather than discretionary shopping, which keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is consistently near +20 to +21 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains at or above +20 while RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average over the next month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PARKS mobility from its already negative level indicates weather or calendar conditions that also discourage leisure shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should soften over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS drops below -22 after staying above -21 for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remains near -20 to -21 in the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS falls below -22 and RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising WORKPLACES mobility and stable-to-falling TRANSIT mobility implies more localized commuting and less shared public travel, which should convert into more neighborhood retail visits within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -20.6 to -11.7 while TRANSIT stayed near zero to slightly negative
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES keeps rising while TRANSIT stays near its current level and RETAIL_REC still fails to improve over four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During reopening, a rebound in PARKS and TRANSIT together indicates broad relaxation of movement constraints; that broader mobility normalization should lift retail-and-recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -18 while TRANSIT rises above 0 in the same week
failure_condition: If both PARKS and TRANSIT cross their thresholds together but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If residential time stays elevated while parks and transit remain weak, people are substituting away from out-of-home discretionary activity, so RETAIL_REC should stay below the prior four-week average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above +4 while PARKS and TRANSIT remain negative and RETAIL_REC nevertheless rises over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
